title.narrative: Strengthened mechanisms for social dialogue, labour inspection, collective bargaining and dispute resolution

description.narrative:
Namibia has a well-established legal and tripartite framework for labour inspection, social dialogue, collective bargaining, and dispute resolution institutionalized through bodies such as the Labour Advisory Council (LAC), Office of the Labour Commissioner, National Coordination Mechanisms for decent work in the fisheries sector, National, Sectoral and enterprise committees, the OSH and Labour Inspectorates in the Ministry of Justice and Labour Relations.
Impact is however limited as there is uneven coverage (especially in informal and high-risk sectors), capacity limitations of institutions and social partners and implementation and enforcement gaps. There is growing progress through sector-focused initiatives (notably fisheries, domestic work, et al) and digital and legislative reforms, but sustained investment in capacity building, inspection systems, and inclusive social dialogue remains critical.
Collective bargaining coverage is uneven, and weaker in informal economy, SMEs and some key sectors like fisheries; dispute resolution system is beset by weak case management and backlogs; OSH and labour inspection systems are under-resourced.
The ILO supports Namibia to strengthen collective bargaining systems, labour dispute prevention and resolution mechanisms, labour and OSH inspections inspectorates and inclusive social dialogue processes. The strategy includes policy advice, support to legislative reforms, and capacity-building for social partners to enhance their participation in tripartite and sectoral dialogue structures. This includes strengthening OSH governance, coordination and labour inspection frameworks in high-risk sectors such as fisheries, ensuring better enforcement of labour standards. Through these interventions, capacities of employers’ and workers’ organizations are enhanced to effectively engage in social dialogue, address labour relations challenges, and advance decent work outcomes across Namibia’s key economic sectors.
